title: Case: Recipient can no longer take a Thursday sofa delivery
context: DL-1297 is a two-person crew delivery booked for Thursday 11 March 2027. Yarrowdale has listed the crew slots that are open if the booking has to move. The recipient left a voicemail on Sunday evening.
initial_request: [Voicemail, Sunday 19:42] Hi, it's Bettany Brackley about the sofa, D L nine five nine. Um, Thursday's no good any more, work's sending me away. Can you make it Tuesday afternoon instead, I'll be in from about one. Cheers, bye.

Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Monday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.
My parcel DL-11136 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.
DL-47701 rebooked for Friday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

DL-1297 (corner sofa, two-person crew) is booked Thursday 2027-03-11, 12:00-16:00. If the customer needs to move it, crew slots open right now are Tuesday 2027-03-09 PM, Tuesday 2027-03-16 PM and Friday 2027-03-19 AM. We need the exact date from the customer. We do not hold slots provisionally and we do not move a crew booking twice.
Yarrowdale has your sofa, DL-1297, booked with a two-person crew for Thursday 11 March between 12:00 and 16:00. If that stops working for you, tell me and I will ask Yarrowdale what else is open.

[Voicemail, Sunday 19:42] Hi, it's Bettany Brackley about the sofa, D L nine five nine. Um, Thursday's no good any more, work's sending me away. Can you make it Tuesday afternoon instead, I'll be in from about one. Cheers, bye.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask which Tuesday he means: 9 March or 16 March.
Call back and ask which Tuesday he means: 9 March or 16 March.

must: Asks Bettany Brackley which Tuesday he means, giving both dates (9 March and 16 March 2027)
States or implies that the booking has not been moved yet
Sends nothing to Yarrowdale until the date is known
must_not: Asks Yarrowdale to move DL-1297 to Tuesday 9 March, or to Tuesday 16 March, without the recipient confirming the date
Tells Bettany Brackley that the delivery has been moved or that a Tuesday slot is confirmed or held
Promises an exact arrival time such as 13:00
Asks for anything other than the date, such as a door code, a reason for the trip or payment details
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: Thanks for your voicemail about DL-1297. Yarrowdale has a crew slot open on two Tuesday afternoons: Tuesday 9 March and Tuesday 16 March. Which one do you want? Nothing has been moved yet and slots are not held, so please reply as soon as you can and I will ask Yarrowdale for that date.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-306: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 6 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
